title: Localization comparison on an affine open
statement: Let $Y$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $\mathcal L$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module], let $s\in\Gamma(Y,\mathcal L)$, and let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. For an open subscheme $W\subseteq Y$ and $n\ge0$ let $\mathcal L|_W^{\otimes n}$ be the tensor power of [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], and for $n<0$ put $\mathcal L|_W^{\otimes n}=(\mathcal L|_W^{\vee})^{\otimes(-n)}$ with $\mathcal L^{\vee}$ the dual of [def-sc-invertible-module]. For $p\ge0$ set $H^p_*(W,\mathcal L,\mathcal F)=\bigoplus_{n\in\mathbb Z}H^p(W,\mathcal F|_W\otimes\mathcal L|_W^{\otimes n})$ [pqf-def-cohomology], a graded module over the graded ring $\Gamma_*(W,\mathcal L)=\bigoplus_{n\ge0}\Gamma(W,\mathcal L^{\otimes n})$ via tensor product and multiplication of sections, and let $H^p_*(W,\mathcal L,\mathcal F)_{(s)}$ be the degree-zero part of its localization at the homogeneous element $s|_W$ of degree $1$, i.e. the module of fractions $\xi/s^n$ with $n\ge0$ and $\xi$ homogeneous of degree $n$. Let $W_s=W\cap Y_s$, with $Y_s$ the open subscheme where $s$ does not vanish [def-weil-pbc-ample-invertible-module], and let $c^p_W:H^p_*(W,\mathcal L,\mathcal F)_{(s)}\to H^p(W_s,\mathcal F|_{W_s})$ be the canonical map sending $\xi/s^n$ to $s^{-n}\xi$ (restrict $\xi$ to $W_s$, where $s^n$ is a trivializing section of $\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$, and divide by it). Then for every $p\ge0$ the map $c^p_Y:H^p_*(Y,\mathcal L,\mathcal F)_{(s)}\to H^p(Y_s,\mathcal F|_{Y_s})$ is an isomorphism, and for $p>0$ both groups are zero.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09MR (coherent-lemma-invert-s-cohomology), proof, affine case; tags 01XB, 01PV, 01PW

proof.text: Because $Y$ is affine, [lem-sc-affine-cap-section-open] applied with $U=Y$ shows that the principal nonvanishing open $Y_s=Y\cap Y_s$ is affine.

For every integer $n$, the sheaf $\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes n}$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-sc-invertible-tensor-qcoherent], so [pqf-lem-affine-vanishing] gives $H^p(Y,\mathcal F\otimes\mathcal L^{\otimes n})=0$ for $p>0$. The restriction $\mathcal F|_{Y_s}$ is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits], and Step 1 plus [pqf-lem-affine-vanishing] gives $H^p(Y_s,\mathcal F|_{Y_s})=0$ for $p>0$. Therefore the graded direct sum and its localization have zero degree-$p$ part for $p>0$, and the target is zero as well.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 09MR proof, affine-open paragraph (using Tag 01XB)

proof.text: In degree $p=0$, the canonical map is an isomorphism by [lem-sc-affine-section-localization], which is the section-localization theorem of [01PW]. Its map sends each homogeneous fraction $\xi/s^n$ to the section $s^{-n}\xi$ on $Y_s$, exactly the map $c^0_Y$ in the statement.

lean.statement: theorem affine_cohomology_localization (Y : Scheme.{uAffine}) [IsAffine Y] (L : Y.Modules) [L.IsInvertible] (s : Γ(L, ⊤)) (F : Y.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] : ∃ U : Y.Opens, (U : Set Y) = nonvanishingLocus L s ∧ ∀ p : ℕ, (∃ e : CohomologyFractionPresentation L F s p ⊤ ≃+ (RingedSpace.openModuleCohomology Y.toRingedSpace p U).obj F, ∀ (n : ℕ) (t : (RingedSpace.openModuleCohomology Y.toRingedSpace p ⊤).obj (F ⊗ L.tensorPow n : Y.Modules)), (RingedSpace.openModuleCohomology Y.toRingedSpace p U).map (((ρ_ F).inv ≫ F ◁ tensorPowSection (homOfGlobalSection L s) n) : F ⟶ (F ⊗ L.tensorPow n : Y.Modules)) (e (cohomologyFraction L F s p ⊤ n t)) = (RingedSpace.openModuleCohomologyRestriction Y.toRingedSpace p (homOfLE (le_top : U ≤ ⊤))).app (F ⊗ L.tensorPow n : Y.Modules) t) ∧ (0 < p → Subsingleton (CohomologyFractionPresentation L F s p ⊤) ∧ Subsingleton ((RingedSpace.openModuleCohomology Y.toRingedSpace p U).obj F))
